column8: Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2 store, answers Q7b Gap 8: a 26 Apr 1979 check paid on 14 May would have been 12 business days late, past the five-day line; fix: no source dates any single check, so say the worst could have crossed it, never that it did, and say whose payment (book entry, Laura's channel, was paid on time, Q15-015).

Wed 18 Nov: store and Table 3 row 2's note at most: CRS's $125,000 forgone on $122 million at over 9% implies about four days on average (Keel arithmetic); fix: the $125,000 rests on a self-published 2012 book CRS cites, so say a few days at most or drop the average; never about four days as a sourced fact.
Wed 18 Nov: Q15-015 already carries the 1979 causes and the $32.5 billion headroom read at CRS; this is Marron's paraphrase of a paywalled paper.
Wed 18 Nov: store, context for row 1: the 1979 surge (tenders up 379%) broke the retail paper channel, not book entry, where Laura's holdings sit.
Wed 18 Nov: store for Table 3 row 3's debt-limit watch: in 1979 a lapsed limit stopped new borrowing (sales postponed, savings bonds suspended), never a payment; read in Treasury's FY1979 report.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: an official annual report silent on the late checks; OCR text search, trivia that serves no part.

Wed 18 Nov: store guard for 3e: the 1979 delay was not public until 8-9 May, so it did not cause the 60bp rise; drop the 60bp from Q65-033 and never cite Zivney and Marcus's cost; both CRS texts read at source.
Wed 18 Nov: the other half of row 7's correction (CPI news, money supply and the FOMC call moved yields on 26-27 Apr 1979); row 7 carries it.
Wed 18 Nov: Q15-015 already has no authority to reimburse and the settled class action; this adds dates and the reported 80% take-up, store only.
Wed 18 Nov: store guard: H.R. 6054 died in committee, so no law made 1979's holders whole (Q15-016 stays refused); with row 14 it backs no interest for a delay.
Wed 18 Nov: the same correction as row 10; never repeat Marron's new legislation or CBS's back interest.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2's definition: a Treasury has no default clause and no grace period (CRS), so the five-day line had to come from outside; it is the report's definition in S&P's words (Q8b-028), never the IPS's; quote CRS, not CBS's unnamed officials.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2's note: 31 CFR 356.30 is the legal source of or the next business day; cite it for Treasury payments only, since IBTQ's Saturday end is a fund date (NUMBERS takes Mon 17 Dec 2035), not this rule.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir with row 15: a late Treasury pays its face, late, and nothing more unless Congress acts (28 USC 2516(a)); read at DOJ.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or Table 3 row 2's note, one clause: the payments' standard (paid even if cash waiting earns nothing, NUMBERS l.2228) already prices an unpaid-for delay at nothing, so a delay before 1 January is a date risk, never a dollar risk; the range's ends are counted undiscounted the same way (NUMBERS 0).
Wed 18 Nov: the 2011 form of Q15-019's on-time principle; adds that principal is paid by rolling into new issues, store only.
Wed 18 Nov: the coupon half of the same plan in Q15-019; the legal authority to prioritise is disputed.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2 store: the Fed drew the delay-default line by cause (political impasse, not inability), Table 3 by days, and both treat a short political delay as no loss to holders; a staff view the FOMC found acceptable, not a rule.
Wed 18 Nov: store for Table 3's watch: the two routes past paying bondholders first (political limits, failed auctions) would both show in public notices; one participant's view.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2's Never: a forced sale: Treasury's 2013 plan rolls a late Treasury one day at a time and it stays transferable on Fedwire, so nothing has to be sold; the Fed's own account, firmer than TMPG's Q15-017.
Wed 18 Nov: store: Treasury decides each evening, with a 10 pm New York deadline; fix the use column: the decision is Treasury's each night, never that Laura learns of it the night before.
Wed 18 Nov: store with row 18: the 2013 test, paid in full and in relatively short order; the authorities put no number on short, so Table 3's five days is one reading of it.
Wed 18 Nov: TMPG's day-by-day roll is Q15-017; the new point, that no official plan counts days, is carried by rows 18 and 32.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e's custody line and Table 3 row 2: a broker need not advance a late Treasury's cash, so money arrives when Treasury pays; no broker's own policy read.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the market's playbook treats a systems failure and a political delay alike, which fits Table 3 counting days; call times are detail, never prose.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3a and Table 3: no cross default between maturities, so one date's delay is one date, not ten; SIFMA's draft assumptions, never a rule; never say later rungs are safe from a delay on their own dates.
Wed 18 Nov: store: a same-day hold paid by the close is not late, so Table 3 row 2's paid when due already covers it; nothing to change.
Wed 18 Nov: store for Table 3 row 2's Never: a forced sale: in SIFMA's worst draft scenario a late Treasury can only be held, not sold, and the plan needs no sale; it has never happened.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2's note or store: why a grace line exists at all, ISDA's three business days to avoid technical triggers from human error or disasters; the Definitions read only in a hosted excerpt.
Wed 18 Nov: Moody's 2023 interview restates Q8b-029's missed or delayed definition read at Moody's; a syndicated Reuters copy, store only.

Wed 18 Nov: store: Fitch's RD and D rest on two summaries (Fitch's site blocked); read Fitch's 24 May 2023 release before any use, and keep Fitch as strict as Moody's on the day marked as Keel's reading.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3 row 2's note or 3e reservoir: four day counts side by side show the five-day line was chosen, the most forgiving because reason 2 asks only a re-check; fix: Fitch only as summarised (row 31), and the line is the report's definition in S&P's words (Q8b-028).
Wed 18 Nov: store: the SEC's money-fund rule separates a default by materiality and cause, a third way to draw the line; the clerical-delay reading is Keel's.
Wed 18 Nov: store and Table 3's facts only: the prospectus's debt-ceiling risk text is boilerplate; never quoted in the report's prose, where it would read as a guard on the Treasuries (Book 19).

Wed 18 Nov: Q36-002 and Q15-028 hold the board's power to extend; the silence on a late holding adds little; not a TNA clash: note 2's timing fits is about the 2032 holdings, and a delay is reason 2's event.
Wed 18 Nov: Q3c-010 already quotes the sponsor's approximately two days after the fund ceases trading; Table 3's 3e notes carry the cash window.
Wed 18 Nov: store: BlackRock's cash arm left early-June 2023 maturities; that IBTM's waiting cash would sit clear of a December 2032 X-date is Keel's inference, never said as fact.
Wed 18 Nov: store for Table 3 row 3: a ladder manager stepped around a 2023 X-date in new purchases and sold nothing, as row 3's never a sale ahead of it says; one manager.
Wed 18 Nov: store beside Q16-036: 2023's bill kink in figures (6.881% against 2.614% two days apart); Table 3 row 3 watches the X-date estimate, not the kink.
Wed 18 Nov: an abstract only; Q15-020 already shows money funds leaving at-risk bills in 2013, this adds 2023 at group level.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e or Table 3 row 2, what to watch as 2033 nears; fix: 22-24 Dec is 8-10 days before 1 January (7-9 days in between), and a fund's December payout is not itself a Treasury payment (row 4 watches the fund) while its Treasuries mature months earlier (NUMBERS 3), so this is the worst case of a holding due at the end.

Wed 18 Nov: store or 3e's list of what left Table 3's cells: a payment 2-5 business days late has no named state, though a debt-limit roll's first week already sits under row 3's look-closer level; never a new level or trigger in the table (CANON A34), and the page is full.

Wed 18 Nov: refuse for 3e prose: a limit clause that a short political US default sits under the line is a certainty guard (Book 19; 3e names a US default once); its facts stay in rows 18 and 29-32 for Table 3's notes.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3e's custody line: a bank's plumbing failure (BoNY 1985) is not a Treasury delay, since Treasury had paid when the Reserve Bank credited the bank (Q72-004), so it is never reason 2; its length not read.
